messages:
Anna: bumping thread — customer reported sudden p99 spikes on /v1/embed (US-WEST). They see p95 ~200ms normally, now p99 ~6-9s and a bunch of 429s when calls pile up. customer attached sample curl and client logs.
Devon: thanks — do we know if they hit any auth changes or quota events recently?
Anna: customer says they rotated API keys yesterday and their internal retry logic retried aggressively. They also saw some billing webhook 403s earlier.
Devon: that rings a bell — we rolled token-rotation job at 08:22 UTC that triggered a short auth cache miss window. If SDKs retried synchronously it could amplify queueing on workers.
Liam: grabbing metrics now — watching worker queue_time_ms and requests_in_flight. Pushing a dashboard link: https://console.redwood/metrics/queue?svc=embed-us-west (shared).
Liam: logs show a burst at 08:25:16 with ~2.1k concurrent inflight, queue_time_ms jumped to 4.2s, and the gateway returned 429 with header `x-rw-retry=1` frequently. Also lots of client retries: see header `x-client-retries: 5`.
Anna: customer sample curl (they included):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embed \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" \
  -d '{"input":"lorem ipsum"}'
```
They also pasted SDK snippet showing no jitter/backoff:
```
client.embed({ input }, { retries: 5, backoff: 200 })
```
Devon: ok. Root cause appears to be a tight retry loop after short auth failures + billing 403s => storm of retries => worker saturation => queueing => p99 regression.
Alex: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) patch gateway to enforce per-client concurrency cap (drop new requests once queue_time > 1s) 2) temporarily raise admission limit for embed pool to drain backlog 3) issue customer token refresh guidance and apply temporary credits. Which should we do first?
Liam: do 2) first to avoid dropping customer traffic — increase pool concurrency by 20% for US-WEST embed workers via autoscaler override. I'll run the command.
Liam: `kubectl patch hpa embed-us-west -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 12}}'` — deploying now. deploy-bot: `Config update started: autoscaler minReplicas=12 for embed-us-west (liam_sre)`
deploy-bot: `Config update success: autoscaler minReplicas=12 for embed-us-west (deploy-id: d-8432)`
Liam: pool scaled, watching metrics. queue_time_ms dropped from 4.2s -> 800ms in ~90s. p99 down to ~1.2s.
Anna: while scaling is in flight, Devon can we flip gateway policy to soft-reject very-high-retry clients? maybe throttle by `x-client-retries` header.
Devon: yes — added a short rule on the gateway to reject requests with `x-client-retries>3` for 60s. roll started. deploy-bot: `gateway rule add: reject-retry-count>3 for 60s (devon_runtime)`
Devon: rule active. We're seeing fewer repeats and the ingress rate is smoothing.
Alex: also sending customer an interim note: ask them to reduce retries and implement exponential backoff/jitter. Offer to whitelist while they patch.
Anna: customer patched their client to backoff (they confirmed) and rotated keys properly. They accepted a temporary credit for failed units.
Liam: leaving an action item for eng-runtime: make gateway pluggable to auto-detect retry storms (based on per-key short auth-fail spikes) and apply mitigations automatically.
Devon: follow-ups: 1) SDK: default to exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries for transient auth errors (PR already drafted) 2) Recording playbook: token rotations should set a short coordination window to avoid mass client retries 3) telemetry: emit per-api-key retry histogram to detect storms sooner.
Anna: customer reports p99 back to ~450ms after fixes, closing their case, but keeping this thread for action items.
Alex: creating a short post-incident doc and linking in eng-runbook.
Liam: assigning 2-day ticket to eng-runtime for automation: RW-7631.
Anna: thanks everyone — tagging to close: @devon @liam @alex :thumbsup:
